chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Abu Tahir al-Warraq, from Rabi' ibn Sulayman al-Kazz al-Kazzaz, from a man, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said:

A man said to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him): 'You have turned to Hajj and left Jihad; you found Hajj easier upon you than Jihad, and Allah says, "Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties..."' [the verse].

He said, and Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Read what comes after it.' He said, and he recited: 'The repentant, the worshippers, the praiseworthy...' until he reached the words: '...and those who preserve the limits [of Allah].'
He said, and Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'When these [qualities] become manifest, we will not prefer anything over Jihad.'

key_terms.الْحَافِظُونَ لِحُدُودِ اللَّهِ: Those who preserve the limits of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between Hajj and Jihad according to Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) clarifies that the 'purchase' of lives and properties in Surah At-Tawbah (9:111) is not limited to military sacrifice but encompasses the spiritual disciplines of repentance, worship, and preserving divine limits. This hadith establishes a Shia scholarly view that internal spiritual purification and adherence to Allah's boundaries are foundational acts of Jihad, equal in merit to physical struggle when performed with sincerity.
